page.summary: The cli app is "agi", a Rust terminal coding agent (crate agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary). It runs Local (Ollama, LM Studio), own-key and Managed Cloud modes. Sign-in is a browser device code. Managed Cloud needs Premium or higher; Free and Basic fail closed, while Local and own key need no plan. It also hosts the app-server that VS Code and Desktop use. No signed release is published yet.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `agi` is the terminal coding agent of AGI Workforce. It is a Rust program with a full-screen terminal UI (TUI), a plain line mode (REPL), and a non-interactive `agi exec` / `--print` mode for scripts and CI. Its package description says it is a multi-provider agentic CLI. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:4; apps/cli/README.md:21-28)

**Who uses it.** Developers who work in a repository and want an AI agent in the terminal, including teams that run it in CI/CD. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:21-28). Account features (usage, library, projects, invites) are for signed-in Managed Cloud users only. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:~195-205)

**Role in the product.** The suite doc calls the CLI the "Developer agent surface and Rust engine proving ground", scoped to a workspace or session by default. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:34). The requirements doc lists it fifth in development order, with local transcripts, resume/branch, approvals, shell tools, MCP/plugins/skills/hooks, subagents and review flows. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:1148-1181)

**Developer domain.** The CLI, Desktop Code and VS Code share one host-owned developer-session runtime. CLI sessions are not merged into Web/Mobile/Desktop Cloud chat without an explicit handoff. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md:49; docs/product/requirements.md:1183). The README repeats this: CLI and VS Code share `~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/` and do not join Cloud chat sync. [code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Architecture section)

**Commands.** Primary command `agi`; `agiworkforce` is a backward-compatible alias (second binary). [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:15-21)

This page names no model IDs for that reason.

Plan credit windows are read at compile time from `packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts`. [code] (apps/cli/src/plans.rs:14-16)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Two kinds of sign-in, both through `agi login`.** [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288)

1. **AGI account (device code).** `agi login` with no provider runs `login_agiworkforce`, which calls `oauth::device_code_login`, saves the grant, and sends a device heartbeat. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1051). The CLI POSTs `api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `api:POST /api/auth/device/token` and `api:POST /api/auth/device/refresh` on the web origin; the `surface` it sends must be one the endpoint accepts (`cli`, `vscode` or another listed one). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:69-75, 133, 229; apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016-1018). The user opens the verification page `/auth/device` in a browser and enters a code (example `ZED3-E49H`). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:285-291). The browser target is checked against trusted AGI hosts. [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:309-312 test name)
2. **Own provider key.** `agi login <provider>` prompts for an API key. The accepted list in the error text: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, ollama-cloud, openrouter, nvidia, plus brave or tavily for web search. GitHub Copilot sign-in is refused as unavailable. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288, 1060-1090)

**Where credentials live.** One OS-keyring entry per provider under service `com.agiworkforce.cli.auth`, plus a non-secret index. With `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` they go in an owner-only file. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92-120, 175). The managed token can also come from env `AGIWORKFORCE_JWT`, then the keyring, then a legacy `~/.agiworkforce/auth.toml`. [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:20-22)

**Account identity.** After sign-in the CLI calls `api:GET /api/me` for the plan tier and email, and caches the tier on disk for 5 minutes (`~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml`, 3-second timeout, trusted `*.agiworkforce.com` HTTPS hosts only). [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:264-275; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:1-50, 195-210). `AGI_AUTH_BASE` overrides the device-grant base for a trusted host. [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:287-292)

**Other commands.** `agi logout` signs out of the account; `agi logout --all` also removes every saved provider key after a confirmation; `agi auth-status` reports state. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7275-7300). The README says the sign-in system behind the account is shared with the web app (the endpoints are in apps/web). [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016)

**Sign-in not needed for Local or own key.** README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan." Whether a Local session can start with no account at all is not stated in one line of code I opened. [unknown for the no-account case; code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Subcommands section)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The CLI names its three trust boundaries with `PrivacyMode`: `Local`, `Byok`, `Managed`. Their words for people are "Local", "Your key", "Managed". [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:253-290). Arguments accepted include `local|offline|device`, `byok|cloud-byok|provider`, `managed|agi|agi-cloud|cloud`. [code] (session.rs:~285-294)

| Mode | Meaning in code | Who can use it | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode:local | "no prompt, chat, or file context should leave this device". Providers are Ollama and LM Studio probed on this computer, plus a custom endpoint with no key on a local URL. | Any user, no subscription | [code] (session.rs:~270; apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:69-119; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1835-1855; README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan") |
| mode:own-key | "selected context may be sent directly to the user's configured provider key". Providers: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, mistral, openrouter, nvidia, user-defined OpenAI-compatible endpoints from `[providers.<name>]` in config.toml | Any user with a key; never gated by plan tier | [code] (session.rs:~272; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-935 comment; apps/cli/README.md custom provider section) |
| mode:cloud (`Managed`) | "selected context may be sent through AGI managed cloud"; requests go to `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` with a bearer token, an `Idempotency-Key` header and client-surface headers | Premium (pro) and higher: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise. Free and Basic fail closed | [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:501-551; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-945; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 359) |

**Free and subscribed users, in one table**

| Plan | Local | Own key | Managed Cloud in the CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan:free | yes | yes | no. `can_access_model_for_tier` returns false for Free, Basic and BYOK | 
| plan:basic | yes | yes | no, "Basic can use the economy roster in Web/Mobile/Desktop chat, but not from the CLI" |
| plan:pro (shown as Premium) | yes | yes | yes, economy plus pro-additions models |
| plan:team | yes | yes | yes, as Premium roster |
| plan:max, plan:max_15x (shown as Ultra) | yes | yes | yes, all three slots for Max/Ultra |
| plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise | yes | yes | yes |

Source for the table: [code] (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-960; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:206-215, 244-253; apps/cli/src/plans.rs:96-104; billing-catalog.ts:359). The capability is named `developer_surfaces`, labelled "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code". [code] (billing-catalog.ts:417)

**Subscription link.** The CLI uses the one AGI subscription system: it reads plan and entitlements from `api:GET /api/me`, plan-capability tables from `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts`, credit windows (5 hours, week, month) from `packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts`, and a paywall body from the gateway when quota is exceeded (150 percent of tier quota per the code comment). `pnpm check:protocol-types` keeps the CLI plan table equal to the billing catalog. [code] (apps/cli/src/plans.rs:14-16; apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:309-315; apps/cli/README.md Subcommands). Usage accounting itself happens on the server. [inferred]

**Boundary rules.** Account commands (`usage`, `invite`, `library`, `projects`, ...) run only in Managed and refuse in Local and own-key before any request. [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:4, 212, 900-968; README). A Local chat "stays on this device and is not saved to your account history". [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:111, 1487). The gateway base must be a trusted AGI HTTPS host before the bearer token is attached. [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:465-480)

**Fallback chains.** `-m a,b,c` lists models; on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect the next takes over with the provider switched automatically. Whether a chain can cross from Local into own key or Managed without consent is not established here. [code-doc] (README; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs) [unknown for the consent question]

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
**Rust crates shared with the Desktop (Tauri) app.** Path dependencies in apps/cli/Cargo.toml: `agiworkforce-agent-core`, `-app-server`, `-llm`, `-model-registry`, `-mcp`, `-protocol`, `-sandbox-policy`, `-execpolicy`, `-command-registry`, `-utils-image`, `-worktree`. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:36-46). The Tauri crate also depends on agent-core, execpolicy, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy and worktree. [code] (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32-39). ARCHITECTURE.md says crates/ is "Shared Rust used by both the desktop and the CLI". [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:22)

**Contracts from the TypeScript side.** The CLI compiles in `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` (model catalog), `managed-usage-limits.ts` (credit windows) and equals `billing-catalog.ts` (plan capabilities) via a check. [code] (model_catalog.rs:25; plans.rs:14; README)

**Protocol types.** `crates/agiworkforce-protocol` exports ts-rs bindings into `packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol`; regenerate with `pnpm generate:protocol-types`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5)

**Other apps that use the CLI as their runtime**

- surface:vscode starts `agi app-server` as the local developer-session runtime (README: used by AGI for VS Code); the extension has app-server references in `apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts` among others. [code-doc + code] (apps/cli/README.md Architecture; grep of apps/extension-vscode/src)
- surface:desktop (Electron) bundles its own `agi` for local coding sessions and talks to it with `DeveloperSessionClient` over stdio. [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md Install section; ARCHITECTURE.md:57-64)
- Desktop workspace terminal: `apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts` consumes `apps/cli/src/app_server/workspace_terminal.rs`. [code] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md DESKTOP-ELECTRON-WORKSPACE-TERMINAL-WIRE-01)
- `agi acp` serves the Agent Client Protocol for Zed and JetBrains. [code-doc] (README)

Nothing under `packages/ui/unified-chat` is used by the CLI; the CLI renders its own terminal UI. [inferred]

sections.heading: Build, run and test
sections.markdown:
All commands come from `docs/agent-context/commands.json` (cli block, lines 142-148) unless noted. [code]

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Type-check | `cargo check -p agiworkforce-cli` |
| Unit tests | `cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib` |
| One test | `cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib <test-name>` |
| Release build | `cargo build --release -p agiworkforce-cli` (binary `agi`) |
| Install from source | `cargo install --path apps/cli --bin agi` (README) |
| Notices | `node apps/cli/scripts/generate-third-party-notices.mjs` (and `--check`) |
| Clippy | `cargo clippy -p agiworkforce-desktop -p agiworkforce-cli --lib -- -D warnings -D unsafe-code` (commands.json:21) |

**Run.** `agi` opens the TUI; `agi exec "..."` or `agi --print` run once; `agi --json-events exec ...` writes one JSON object per event; `agi doctor` checks the setup; `agi app-server` serves the local runtime; `agi remote-control` starts a host. [code-doc] (README) / [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6659)

**CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test --locked -p agiworkforce-cli` under `xvfb-run` on Linux, then the workspace lib tests excluding desktop and cli, the app-server and protocol tests, and MCP tests. [code] (.github/workflows/ci.yml:915-918)

**Test layout.** Unit tests are inline in src modules; integration tests are in `apps/cli/tests/` (app_server_stdio, app_server_websocket, app_server_read_only_token, developer_session_host, json_events_jsonl, broken_pipe, init_managed_trust, terminal_escape_diagnostics, plugins and hooks coverage). TUI snapshot files live in `src/tui/snapshots` (insta). [code] (directory listings; Cargo.toml dev-dependencies)

**Local rules.** On the owner's 16 GB machine, cargo builds and full suites run one at a time through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, Delegation section). I ran nothing for this page. No run of these commands is recorded in the documents I read. [unknown]

**Runtime need.** A sandbox backend (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS); `agi doctor` reports `sandbox.os` as a warning when missing. [code-doc] (README)

sections.heading: Release state
sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** The code is broad and connected: the Cargo manifest, command dispatch, auth, managed gateway client, app-server, TUI and REPL are all present (see Folder map). Version is 0.0.1. [code]

**Release status.** [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13) `SURFACE_STATUS` marks only web "Available now"; `cli` is "Coming soon". The public CLI download link is `/download#cli-downloads`. [code] (surface-status.ts:62)

**Pipeline exists, first release unconfirmed.**

- `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml` triggers on tags `v-cli-*` (tag must equal the Cargo version) and on manual runs. A tag run validates, builds six archives (macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Windows x64 and arm64), signs `SHA256SUMS` with a P-256 key held in the protected `cli-release` environment, and publishes a GitHub release. A manual run builds and stops. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/cli-release.md:1-50; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:1-30)
- The binaries have no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; the signed checksum manifest is the integrity check. [requirement] (cli-release.md)
- `apps/web/public/install.sh` pins a public release key (line 31) and stops with "No signed AGI CLI release is published yet" when GitHub answers 404. [code] (install.sh:31-35, 133)
- The README says the installer stops with that message until the first signed release exists. The surface matrix says "Whether it has ever run is not in this tree." [code-doc] [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md; docs/product/suite.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:26). So whether any release is live is [unknown].

**Install channels.** Only the curl installer is advertised; `agi update --install` self-updates; the VS Code extension and Desktop installer bundle or fetch `agi`. Homebrew, npm, WinGet, apt, native Windows installer: none advertised (Homebrew writes to a private tap). [requirement] (cli-release.md, Install channels)

**Verification status.** No document I read records a real end-to-end run of the CLI against production. The audit register records some Electron-to-CLI acceptance work, but it is isolated and not a CLI release check. [unknown / code-doc] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md line 224)

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
| Topic | Unified product (Web/Desktop/Mobile) | CLI | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat history | Account cloud chats sync across apps | Developer sessions in `~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/`, shared only with VS Code; no cloud chat sync, explicit handoff only | [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md:49; README) |
| Managed Cloud access | Cloud chat from Free upward on Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome (capability `managed_chat` covers free to enterprise) | Managed needs Premium or higher (`developer_surfaces`) | [code] (apps/cli/src/plans.rs:93-99; billing-catalog.ts:346, 359) |
| Local mode | Local inference on mobile and desktop is free of a paid subscription | Local (Ollama, LM Studio) and own key are free of plan gating in the CLI; Free users can use them | [code] (model_catalog.rs:915-935) |
| UI | Shared `packages/ui/unified-chat` | Own ratatui TUI and REPL; own slash commands | [inferred] |
| Features absent in the CLI | Research reports, study mode, video, camera, screen capture, connector gallery, app/artifact rendering, library browser, computer-use driving | absent per matrix: research, study, video, camera, screen capture, connectors (it uses MCP), apps rendering, library browser, desktop driving | [requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:197, 277, 287, 317, 337, 347, 357, 407, 517) |
| Fast mode | Provider speed tier | `/fast` switches to a faster model in-session; sends no provider speed field | [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:267) |
| Billing and admin | Web control plane | None in CLI: billing, Team admin, connector setup, Enterprise sales live in Web | [code-doc] (README) |
| Model catalog | One generated catalog | Same `models.json`, compiled in; Free and Basic see no Cloud section in the picker | [code] (model_catalog.rs:915-960) |
| Account-cloud features present in CLI | projects, memory, artifacts, image, shares, devices, library | present under `src/cloud/` | [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:177, 187, 207, 307) |
| Remote control | Mobile steers Desktop/local host | CLI has a `remote-control` command and a module | [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:894, 6659; src/remote_control/) |

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Only read-only checks were done for this page; run nothing below unless you intend to.

1. Build state: `cargo check -p agiworkforce-cli` and `cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib` (commands.json:143-145).
2. Release state: read `SURFACE_STATUS` in apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts; check GitHub for a `v-cli-*` release; run `bash apps/web/public/install.sh` only on a throwaway machine.
3. Plan gate: read `can_access_model_for_tier` in apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs and `developer_surfaces` in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts; run `agi plans` signed in to see which plans include "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code".
4. Sign-in: run `agi login`, then `agi auth-status`; for own key run `agi login <provider>`.
5. Modes: run `agi --privacy local` (or the `--privacy` argument) and `agi doctor` with Ollama running; see apps/cli/src/local_models.rs probes.
6. Doc drift: compare surface-feature-matrix.md cli rows to `pub mod` lines in apps/cli/src/lib.rs.
7. Guards: `pnpm check:protocol-types`, `pnpm check:llm-operability`, and `node apps/cli/scripts/generate-third-party-notices.mjs --check`.

key_facts.fact: The CLI is a Rust crate named agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary, not published to crates.io.
Two binaries: `agi` (primary, default-run) and `agiworkforce` (backward-compatible alias).
main.rs only calls agiworkforce_cli::run_to_exit_code(); the real command dispatch lives in src/lib.rs (about 11,000 lines).
Sign-in to an AGI account uses a browser device code against /api/auth/device/code, /token and /refresh on the web origin.
Credentials are stored in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) with an owner-only file fallback when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1.
The CLI has three trust boundaries in code: PrivacyMode Local, Byok, Managed.
Managed Cloud in the CLI requires the developer_surfaces capability, granted to pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise; Free and Basic fail closed.
Local (Ollama, LM Studio) and own-key modes are never gated by subscription tier, so a Free user can use them.
Managed chat requests go to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions on a trusted AGI HTTPS host with a bearer token and an Idempotency-Key header.
Plan tier is read from GET /api/me and cached in ~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml for 5 minutes with a 3-second timeout.
Account commands (usage, library, projects, invite and others) run only in Managed mode and refuse in Local and own-key mode before any request.
The web release-status table marks the CLI 'Coming soon'; only web is 'Available now'.

A release workflow exists (tags v-cli-*, six archives, signed SHA256SUMS), but the installer says 'No signed AGI CLI release is published yet' on a 404, and the matrix says whether the workflow ever ran is not in the tree.
Binaries carry no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; integrity relies on a signed checksum manifest.
Build and test commands: cargo check/test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib, cargo build --release -p agiworkforce-cli.
CI runs cargo test --locked -p agiworkforce-cli under xvfb-run, then workspace lib tests excluding desktop and cli.
The CLI shares 11 path-dependency crates with the Tauri desktop backend (agent-core, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy, execpolicy, worktree and more).
`agi app-server` is the local developer-session runtime used by VS Code and the Electron Desktop; CLI and VS Code share ~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/ and do not sync into Cloud chat.
The model catalog is compiled in from packages/contracts/types/src/models.json; model IDs are not hardcoded in the CLI.
Sandbox: macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap, none on Windows; no in-process fallback; --no-sandbox is the only workaround.
evidence: apps/cli/README.md Runtime requirement and Sandbox defaults sections

key_facts.fact: Voice (push-to-talk) is an optional Cargo feature off by default because cpal links ALSA on Linux.
The CLI has a remote-control command and module, although the surface matrix reports remote control absent for the CLI.
The CLI plan credit windows are read at compile time from managed-usage-limits.ts; plan labels show pro as Premium and max_15x as Ultra.
Custom OpenAI-compatible providers are added with [providers.<name>] in ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml; names that collide with built-ins are ignored.
The README claims 35 hook events; I did not verify the count in code.
A multi-model fallback chain (-m a,b,c) switches model and provider on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect.
About 4,578 test markers exist under apps/cli/src; this is a grep count, not a run result.
evidence: grep count of #[test] and #[tokio::test] in apps/cli/src

open_questions: Has any signed CLI release ever been published? The tree does not say; the installer reports none and the surface status is Coming soon.
Can Local mode start with no AGI account at all? README says Local and own key need no plan, but I did not find the single code check for the no-account case.
May a fallback chain cross from Local to own key or Managed without a consent step? AGENTS.md requires explicit consent for such moves; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs was not read.
Product choice: should Free and Basic users get any managed model in the CLI? Code excludes them; billing-catalog sets developer_surfaces to PRO_TIERS.
Are the hook events really 35, and are all three MCP transports connected? Only the README states this.
Do the packages ai/providers folders map to CLI providers? The CLI uses the Rust crate agiworkforce-llm, so provider:<package folder> edges are only approximate.
What real verification (manual run, CI results) exists for Managed mode on production? None is recorded in the documents read.
Does the Desktop (Electron) installer currently ship the CLI binary in a released build, given Desktop is also Coming soon?

issues.problem: Plan names are inconsistent. vscode.md says 'Pro-or-higher' and lists 'Pro, Max, Max 15x'. cli.md and the subscriptions page use Premium and Ultra. A reader cannot tell that Pro, Premium and the `pro` tier are one plan, or that Max 15x is Ultra at $200. The execution-boundaries page also mixes 'PRO_TIERS' and 'Premium'.
issues.fix: Use public labels in prose: Premium, Max, Ultra. Show the stored id once in backticks, for example 'Premium (`pro`) or higher'. The set is `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`. Do the same in the cli.md plan table.

issues.problem: The own-key provider list differs inside the page. Line 109 lists 'mistral' and omits minimax and ollama-cloud. Line 92 lists the accepted login ids, which include minimax and ollama-cloud and no mistral.
issues.fix: Use one list taken from API_KEY_PROVIDERS. As of f51d16e747: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, ollama-cloud, openrouter, nvidia, plus brave and tavily for search. Mention 'user-defined OpenAI-compatible endpoints' separately. Remove mistral unless a source is found (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1060-1160). A grep of apps/cli/src finds no mistral.
